  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, adminMode>>

  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, assigned>>

====
nl: A power-grid load shedder assigns load-shed slots to feeders under a leader elected with failover, and a privileged administrator can override the leader. A leadership epoch identifies the current term; an election installs a new leader and bumps the epoch, providing failover. Normally only the current leader assigns a shed slot to a feeder, and it may do so only while that slot is not already assigned. The administrator, while override mode is engaged, may assign a slot directly, bypassing the leader, but still only while the slot is unassigned. The operations are: Elect (a node becomes the new leader and the epoch is bumped, up to a bound), Assign (the current leader assigns a shed slot that is not already taken to a feeder), Release (an assigned shed slot is freed), EngageAdmin (the administrator engages override mode), DisengageAdmin (the administrator disengages override mode), and AdminAssign (while override mode is engaged, the administrator assigns an untaken shed slot to a feeder directly). SAFETY PROPERTY: no load-shed slot is ever assigned to two different feeders at the same time, so the same slot is never double-allocated.

nl: A university course-registration system holds a fixed number of seats in a course and hands them out as time-limited leases to students. Every seat is either available or currently leased; a lease is granted from the available pool and returned to it when the lease expires. Each lease has a remaining time that ticks down and can be renewed. A student may be slow but never fails: while slow it can neither be granted a lease nor renew one, but it always eventually speeds up, so no student is permanently lost. The total number of seats (available plus leased) is fixed. CONSTANTS
    Coordinators = {pa, pb}
    MaxGen = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoStaleAction
nl: A blood-bank inventory tracker commits inventory changes with two-phase commit driven by a coordinator, where coordination is handed off between coordinators over time. A global generation number identifies the current coordination regime; handing coordination to a coordinator bumps the generation and stamps that coordinator's personal generation with the new value. Only the current coordinator may prepare and commit a transaction, and a commit stamps the committed transaction with the committer's personal generation. A former coordinator is stale: its personal generation lags the current generation, so its actions must not be accepted. A coordinator may be slow but never fails: while slow it can neither prepare nor commit, but it always eventually speeds up, so no coordinator is permanently lost. The operations are: HandOff (while idle, coordination passes to a coordinator, bumping the generation and refreshing that coordinator's personal generation), Prepare (the current, non-slow coordinator moves an idle transaction into the prepared phase), Commit (the current, non-slow coordinator commits a prepared transaction, stamping it with its own personal generation), Abort (a prepared transaction is aborted back to idle), Reset (a committed transaction returns to idle, clearing the commit stamp), BecomeSlow (a coordinator becomes temporarily slow), and Speedup (a slow coordinator resumes). SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a transaction is committed, its commit stamp equals the current generation, so no stale former coordinator's commit is ever accepted.

---- MODULE W4Od14m2p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Targets, Drones, MaxLoad

VARIABLES phase, votes, dropLog, retardant

vars == <<phase, votes, dropLog, retardant>>
Ran(s) == {s[i] : i \in DOMAIN s}

TypeOK ==
  /\ phase \in [Targets -> {"idle", "voting", "dropped"}]
  /\ votes \subseteq [target: Targets, drone: Drones]
  /\ dropLog \in Seq(Targets)
  /\ retardant \in 0..MaxLoad

Init ==
  /\ phase = [t \in Targets |-> "idle"]
  /\ votes = {}
  /\ dropLog = << >>
  /\ retardant = MaxLoad

Propose(t) ==
  /\ phase[t] = "idle"
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "voting"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, dropLog, retardant>>

Vote(t, d) ==
  /\ phase[t] = "voting"
  /\ [target |-> t, drone |-> d] \notin votes
  /\ votes' = votes \cup {[target |-> t, drone |-> d]}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, dropLog, retardant>>

CommitDrop(t) ==
  /\ phase[t] = "voting"
  /\ \A d \in Drones : [target |-> t, drone |-> d] \in votes
  /\ t \notin Ran(dropLog)
  /\ retardant > 0
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "dropped"]
  /\ dropLog' = Append(dropLog, t)
  /\ retardant' = retardant - 1
  /\ votes' = {v \in votes : v.target # t}

Abort(t) ==
  /\ phase[t] = "voting"
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
  /\ votes' = {v \in votes : v.target # t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<dropLog, retardant>>

Reignite(t) ==
  /\ phase[t] = "dropped"
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![t] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, dropLog, retardant>>

Refill ==
  /\ retardant < MaxLoad
  /\ retardant' = retardant + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, votes, dropLog>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Targets: Propose(t)
  \/ \E t \in Targets, d \in Drones: Vote(t, d)
  \/ \E t \in Targets: CommitDrop(t)
  \/ \E t \in Targets: Abort(t)
  \/ \E t \in Targets: Reignite(t)
  \/ Refill

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

DropAtMostOnce == Cardinality(Ran(dropLog)) = Len(dropLog)
====
nl: A wildfire drone surveillance swarm decides where to drop fire retardant using two-phase commit across the drones. Dropping retardant on a target is irreversible and must happen at most once per target, ever. For each target a proposal opens, the drones cast approving votes, and the drop commits only once every drone has approved. Approval messages travel over a channel that can reorder them, so votes are collected into an unordered set keyed by target and drone. A target may reignite after a drop and become eligible for proposals again, but it must never be dropped a second time. Retardant is drawn from a shared tank that can be refilled. Every drop is recorded in an append-only drop log. The operations are: Propose (an idle target enters the voting phase), Vote (a drone casts an approving vote for a voting target, added to the unordered vote set), CommitDrop (a voting target that every drone has approved, that has never been dropped before, and for which tank retardant remains, is dropped once: it is appended to the drop log, the tank is decremented, and its votes are cleared), Abort (a voting target returns to idle and its votes are cleared), Reignite (a previously dropped target becomes idle again and eligible for future proposals), and Refill (the shared retardant tank is replenished by one). SAFETY PROPERTY: the drop log never records the same target in two different positions, so retardant is dropped on each target at most once.

nl: A stock exchange opening auction accepts orders only from participants that hold the required hierarchical locks: a single coarse market lock must be acquired first, then a fine per-symbol lock, before any order may be submitted for that symbol. Only a participant holding both the coarse lock and the fine lock for a symbol is authorized to submit an order for it; a participant that holds neither, or that never acquired them, is unauthorized and must not have its orders accepted. Any participant may crash silently and stop acting, keeping whatever locks it held until it recovers. Releasing the coarse lock finalizes and clears that participant's in-flight orders and drops all of its fine locks. The operations are: AcquireCoarse (a non-crashed participant takes the single coarse market lock when it is free), AcquireFine (a non-crashed participant holding the coarse lock takes the fine lock on one symbol), Submit (a non-crashed participant holding both the coarse lock and a symbol's fine lock submits an order for that symbol), ReleaseAll (a non-crashed participant holding the coarse lock releases it together with all of its fine locks, clearing its in-flight orders), Crash (a not-yet-crashed participant crashes silently while keeping its locks), and Recover (a crashed participant restarts). SAFETY PROPERTY: every in-flight submitted order belongs to a participant that currently holds both the coarse market lock and the fine lock for that order's symbol, so no unauthorized or stale participant's order is ever accepted.
